questions.text: Write the basic functional units of computer.
What is a bus? What are the different buses in a CPU?
What is instruction register?
Give the CPU performance equation.
What is RAM? What is its significance?
What is pipelining?
How is cache memory used to reduce the execution time?

questions.topic: Secondary memories (optical, magnetic tape, magnetic disks, controllers)
questions.text: Write short notes on: (a) Define hit ratio. (b) Optical drives.
What are data transfer techniques?
Define DMA.
Define addressing mode and explain the different types of basic addressing modes with an example.
State the CPU performance equation and the factors that affect performance.
Multiply the following pair of signed 2's complement numbers: A = 010111, B = 101100.
Explain how the instruction pipeline works. What are the various situations where an instruction pipeline can stall? Illustrate with an example.
Define control transfer in CPU.
Explain the basic concepts of fetching cycle and compare it with sequence processing with a neat diagram.

A block-set associative cache consists of 128 blocks divided into four-block sets. Main memory has 16,384 blocks of 256 eight-bit words each. (1) How many bits address main memory? (2) How many bits for TAG, SET and WORD?
Explain the various mapping techniques associated with cache memories.
Explain with a block diagram the DMA transfer in a computer system.
Describe in detail input and output organization.

questions.text: Differentiate between Computer Architecture and Organization.
What is instruction register?
A pipeline consists of 4 stages with a clock cycle time of 5 ns. Calculate the time required to execute 10 instructions.
What is ALU?
What are the differences between hardwired and micro-programmed control units?
Draw the flow of instruction cycle.
Draw the basic structure of memory hierarchy.
An associative memory has 64 words and each word has 16 bits. Calculate the total memory capacity in bytes.
A DMA system transfers 512 bytes from an I/O device to memory. If the bus transfer rate is 4 MB/s, calculate the time required.
Differentiate between synchronous and asynchronous data transfer techniques.
Define addressing mode and explain the different types of basic addressing modes with an example.
Explain memory hierarchy in brief. A word-addressable computer has 1 GB of memory and a 64-bit word. Assuming 80 control lines and 40 interrupt lines, how large is the system bus?
(i) Tabulate the difference between RISC and CISC. (ii) State rules for floating point addition.
Explain the basic concepts of pipelining and compare it with serial processing with a neat diagram.

Explain the concept of hardwired control unit. A micro-programmed control unit has 2 KB control memory, 20-bit microinstructions, 1 µs per microinstruction; a program needs 50 microinstructions. Find capacity, time, control memory size in bytes, and speedup if hardwired takes 30 µs.
Explain the steps involved in instruction interpretation and execution with a simple instruction like ADD R1, R2.

Explain the concept of cache memory. A four-block cache (initially empty) gets block references 4,5,7,12,4,5,13,4,5,7. Find hit ratio using FIFO, LRU, direct mapped, and two-way set associative with LRU.
What is a bus interface? Discuss its role in coordinating communication between CPU, memory and I/O devices. Differentiate between I/O channels and I/O processors.
What is DMA? Explain DMA operation with a suitable figure. A 1 MBPS I/O device on a 32-bit processor in cycle-stealing DMA transfers 8 words in 1 µs. What percentage of time is the CPU blocked?

questions.text: How does the CPU communicate with I/O devices?
Write the full form of ASCII.
Write the concept of Von Neumann architecture.
Name the two signals generated by the memory.
What are an accumulator and a program counter?
A CPU has 32-bit instructions and a program starts at 200. What is a legal value of the program counter (byte-addressable memory)? (a) 226 (b) 242 (c) 246 (d) 252
Differentiate between RISC and CISC.
Design a computer system with block diagram.
What do you mean by single precision and double precision? Draw the instruction format for both.
Write down the value formation for 32-bit IEEE 754 standard for the number 01000001111000----0000.

Explain in detail the concept of addressing mode. An instruction is stored at location 300 with address field at 301 holding 250; a processor register holds 200. Evaluate the effective address for 5 kinds of addressing.
Explain the basic concept of pipelining.
What are the types of address instructions? Perform X = (A-B)/(C*D) for any two formats.
Explain memory instruction and instruction sequence.
What is the full form of RISC? Explain it briefly.
What is a bus? What are the different types of buses? Explain in one line.
What are the different computer generations? Explain each in one line.
What is an instruction? Draw the instruction format.
What are the different types of computers based on size, power and functionality? Explain each in one line.
Convert decimal 153 to binary and give its 1's and 2's complement.
Draw Von Neumann architecture.
What are the different functional units of a computer system? Explain each in one line.
Which combinational hardware device is used when data is transferred from a register to the common bus? Explain why and its basic function.
Convert binary 110110101 to decimal.
Draw the accumulator-based processor architecture and explain its components in detail.
Perform arithmetic operations on integers: 15+10, 111+22, 10-8, 10*11, 16/2.
(A) With 32-bit addresses, how many locations are possible with 16-bit addressing? Size of memory in GB. (B) Represent 1.25 in IEEE single-precision (32-bit) format.
What are the different addressing modes? Explain each briefly with a memory-mapping diagram and examples.

questions.topic: Secondary memories (optical, magnetic tape, magnetic disks, controllers)
questions.text: The dots on the magnetic tape represent: (a) binary digits (b) decimal digits (c) hex digits (d) octal digits
Select all components involved in the control unit: (a) micro-programmed control (b) hardwired control (c) pipelining (d) ALU
Match memory types (associative, cache, virtual, secondary) with characteristics (non-volatile, speeds access, content-addressed, extends main memory).
Differentiate between hardwired and micro-programmed control unit.
4 page frames, initially empty; reference string 4,7,6,1,7,6,1,2,7,2. Total page faults with (a) LRU (b) FIFO.
Define and outline the steps in fetch cycle.
What is the purpose of cache memory, and how does it differ from main memory?
125 control signals in 5 mutually exclusive groups (20, 70, 2, 10, 23). Control word size for horizontal and vertical microprogramming, and bits saved.
256 KB 4-way set-associative cache, 32-byte blocks, 32-bit physical address. Find tag bits, showing each step.
